## README [¶](#section-readme "Go to Readme")

### Glamour

![Glamour Title Treatment](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23aabf2a-8bd8-4e7b-bb50-993bce32541d)

Stylesheet-based markdown rendering for your CLI apps.

![Glamour example](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec2ead40-c467-48cc-b6a8-f0f13709eeab)

`glamour` lets you render [markdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markdown) documents & templates on [ANSI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code) compatible terminals. You can create your own stylesheet or simply use one of the stylish defaults.

#### Usage

```
import "github.com/charmbracelet/glamour" in := `# Hello World This is a simple example of Markdown rendering with Glamour! Check out the [other examples](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/tree/master/examples) too. Bye! ` out, err := glamour.Render(in, "dark") fmt.Print(out) 
```

![Hello World example](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/raw/master/examples/helloworld/helloworld.png)

##### Custom Renderer

```
import "github.com/charmbracelet/glamour" r, _ := glamour.NewTermRenderer( // detect background color and pick either the default dark or light theme glamour.WithAutoStyle(), // wrap output at specific width (default is 80) glamour.WithWordWrap(40), ) out, err := r.Render(in) fmt.Print(out) 
```

#### Styles

You can find all available default styles in our [gallery](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/tree/master/styles/gallery). Want to create your own style? [Learn how!](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/tree/master/styles)

There are a few options for using a custom style:

1. Call `glamour.Render(inputText, "desiredStyle")`
2. Set the `GLAMOUR_STYLE` environment variable to your desired default style or a file location for a style and call `glamour.RenderWithEnvironmentConfig(inputText)`
3. Set the `GLAMOUR_STYLE` environment variable and pass `glamour.WithEnvironmentConfig()` to your custom renderer

#### Glamourous Projects

Check out these projects, which use `glamour`:

* [Glow](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glow), a markdown renderer for the command-line.
* [GitHub CLI](https://github.com/cli/cli), GitHub’s official command line tool.
* [GitLab CLI](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli), GitLab's official command line tool.
* [Gitea CLI](https://gitea.com/gitea/tea), Gitea's official command line tool.
* [Meteor](https://github.com/odpf/meteor), an easy-to-use, plugin-driven metadata collection framework.

common questions

 glow is a terminal Markdown reader/browser written in Go by Charmbracelet. It uses the Glamour rendering engine and supports both TUI file browsing and direct CLI rendering.
 glow uses Charmbracelet's own Glamour engine to render Markdown into styled ANSI output.
 Yes. glow supports fetching and rendering Markdown directly from a URL, which is handy for quick README previews.
 Yes. glow auto-detects the terminal theme and selects light/dark styles by default. Custom styles are also supported.
 Yes. glow has built-in GitHub repository support and can fetch and render a repo's README directly.

installation and configuration [...] Custom Styles

If built-in themes aren't enough, you can load custom JSON style files. Glamour's style system offers fine-grained control: heading levels, code block highlighting, blockquote styling, list indentation, link colors, and more.

bash

```
glow -s mystyle.json document.md glow -s mystyle.json document.md
```

The Charm team maintains a style gallery with community-contributed themes ranging from minimal to fancy.

Output Control

bash

```
# Control line width (defaults to terminal width)# Control line width (defaults to terminal width)glow -w 80 document.md glow -w  80 document.md # Use external pager (defaults to less -r)# Use external pager (defaults to less -r)glow -p document.md glow -p document.md

Case 3: Formatting Emails or Reports

Writing a Markdown-formatted email and want to preview before sending:

bash

```
cat draft.md | glow - cat draft.md  |  glow -
```

The terminal preview closely matches the final rendered output.

## glow: A Markdown Reader Built for the Terminal [​](#glow-a-markdown-reader-built-for-the-terminal)

Ever find yourself staring at README files in the terminal, but don't want to open a browser or a heavy editor just to read them? glow is a terminal-based Markdown reader that transforms plain text files into beautifully formatted, easy-to-read documents—all within your command line.

Developed by the Charm team in Go, glow is built on their own Glamour rendering engine. It's not just a simple Markdown-to-text converter—it offers an interactive TUI interface, automatic discovery of local documents, and the ability to fetch and render Markdown directly from GitHub, GitLab, or any URL.

## Two Usage Modes: TUI Browser and CLI Tool [​](#two-usage-modes-tui-browser-and-cli-tool)

glow follows a "use it however you want" philosophy. Run it without arguments to launch a beautiful text-based user interface; provide a file path and it renders directly to your terminal.

**TUI Mode: Local Document Browser**

Running `glow` without arguments launches a full-screen interface that scans for Markdown files in the current directory and its subdirectories. If you're in a Git repository, it recursively searches the entire repo. Navigate with keyboard shortcuts: arrow keys to select files, Enter to open, `?` for help, and familiar `less`-like controls for reading.

This mode is perfect for browsing project documentation. Large projects often have sprawling docs directories—glow's list view lets you quickly locate files, while its built-in pager provides a smooth reading experience.

**CLI Mode: Flexible Document Rendering**

bash

```
# Render local file # Render local fileglow README.md glow README.md # Read from stdin # Read from stdinecho "# Hello World" | glow - echo  "# Hello World"  |  glow - # Open a GitHub repository's README directly # Open a GitHub repository's README directlyglow github.com/charmbracelet/glow glow github.com/charmbracelet/glow # Fetch Markdown from a URL # Fetch Markdown from a URLglow https://example.com/doc.md glow https://example.com/doc.md
```

This flexibility lets glow integrate seamlessly into various workflows. Use it as a Markdown formatter with pipes, or set up aliases for quick access to documentation.

## Styling and Rendering: More Than Just "Colors" [​](#styling-and-rendering-more-than-just-colors)

glow's rendering quality is its core strength. Built on the Glamour engine, it supports the full CommonMark specification with extensive optimizations for terminal output.

**Automatic Theme Detection**

By default, glow detects your terminal's current background color (dark or light) and automatically selects an appropriate color scheme. You can also specify manually:

bash

```
glow -s dark # Force dark theme glow -s  dark  # Force dark themeglow -s light # Force light theme glow -s  light  # Force light theme
```

**Custom Styles**

If built-in themes aren't enough, you can load custom JSON style files. Glamour's style system offers fine-grained control: heading levels, code block highlighting, blockquote styling, list indentation, link colors, and more.

bash

```
glow -s mystyle.json document.md glow -s mystyle.json document.md
```

The Charm team maintains a [style gallery](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/blob/master/styles/gallery/README.md) with community-contributed themes ranging from minimal to fancy.

**Output Control**

bash

```
# Control line width (defaults to terminal width)# Control line width (defaults to terminal width)glow -w 80 document.md glow -w  80 document.md # Use external pager (defaults to less -r)# Use external pager (defaults to less -r)glow -p document.md glow -p document.md
```

The `-w` flag is useful when reading code-heavy documents—preventing overly long lines. The `-p` flag hands output to your system's `$PAGER`, ideal for very long documents.

## Configuration File: No More Repetitive Flags [​](#configuration-file-no-more-repetitive-flags)

If you find yourself using the same flags repeatedly, create a configuration file. Run `glow config` to open it in your `$EDITOR`, or manually create `glow.yml` in your platform's default config path:

yaml

```
# Style: auto, dark, light, or path to JSON file# Style: auto, dark, light, or path to JSON filestyle: "auto" style: "auto" # Enable mouse wheel in TUI mode # Enable mouse wheel in TUI modemouse: true mouse: true # Use pager by default # Use pager by defaultpager: true pager: true # Default word wrap width # Default word wrap widthwidth: 80 width: 80 # Show all files (including hidden and gitignored)# Show all files (including hidden and gitignored)all: false all: false # Show line numbers in TUI mode # Show line numbers in TUI modeshowLineNumbers: false showLineNumbers: false # Preserve original newlines (default reflows text)# Preserve original newlines (default reflows text)preserveNewLines: false preserveNewLines: false
```

Config paths vary by platform: macOS typically uses `~/Library/Application Support/glow/`, Linux follows XDG conventions, and Windows uses `%APPDATA%\glow\`. Run `glow --help` to see the exact path for your system.

## Real-World Use Cases [​](#real-world-use-cases)

**Case 1: Quick Project Documentation Review**

Just cloned a new project and want to understand its structure:

bash

```
cd new-project cd new-project glow glow# Navigate with arrow keys, Enter to read, q to return, Q to quit# Navigate with arrow keys, Enter to read, q to return, Q to quit
```

**Case 2: Reading Remote Documentation**

Found an interesting README on GitHub but don't want to clone the entire repository:

bash

```
glow github.com/owner/repo glow github.com/owner/repo
```

glow automatically fetches and renders the repository's default README.

**Case 3: Formatting Emails or Reports**

Writing a Markdown-formatted email and want to preview before sending:

bash

```
cat draft.md | glow - cat draft.md  |  glow -
```

The terminal preview closely matches the final rendered output.

## Installation [​](#installation)

**Via x-cmd** (recommended):

bash

```
x env use glow x  env  use  glow
```

**macOS / Linux**:

bash

```
brew install glow brew  install  glow
```

**Arch Linux**:

bash

```
pacman -S glow pacman -S  glow
```

**Nix**:

bash

```
nix-shell -p glownix-shell -p  glow
```

**Go install** (requires Go 1.21+):

bash

```
go install github.com/charmbracelet/glow/v2@latest go  install github.com/charmbracelet/glow/v2@latest
```

**Other platforms**:

Windows users can use Chocolatey, Scoop, or Winget: `choco install glow`, `scoop install glow`, or `winget install charmbracelet.glow`. FreeBSD uses `pkg install glow`, Void Linux uses `xbps-install -S glow`, and Solus uses `eopkg install glow`. Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL users need to add Charm's official repository—see the GitHub repo for specific commands.

## Wrapping Up [​](#wrapping-up)

glow solves a seemingly simple but often overlooked problem: how to read documents elegantly in a terminal environment. Its design avoids over-complication—the TUI mode is intuitive, the CLI mode is flexible, and the rendering quality is solid. For developers who spend significant time in the terminal, it's a "just right" tool.

The Charm team's series of tools (bubbletea, bubbles, glamour, etc.) all pursue the same goal: giving command-line applications a modern user experience. glow is a great embodiment of this philosophy. If you're still using `cat README.md` or constantly switching to your browser for documentation, give glow a try—it might become a default tool in your workflow.

**Source:**

<https://github.com/charmbracelet/glow>

<https://charm.sh/>

## FAQ

**common questions**

* glow is a terminal Markdown reader/browser written in Go by Charmbracelet. It uses the Glamour rendering engine and supports both TUI file browsing and direct CLI rendering.
* glow uses Charmbracelet's own Glamour engine to render Markdown into styled ANSI output.
* Yes. glow supports fetching and rendering Markdown directly from a URL, which is handy for quick README previews.
* Yes. glow auto-detects the terminal theme and selects light/dark styles by default. Custom styles are also supported.
* Yes. glow has built-in GitHub repository support and can fetch and render a repo's README directly.

**installation and configuration**

* On macOS use `x brew install glow`; on Linux use `x apt/dnf install glow`; on Windows use `x scoop install glow`. Refer to the upstream README for the exact command.
* glow reads a configuration file from the user directory where you can customize styles and default behavior (refer to official docs for the exact path).
* Yes. The TUI mode of glow has mouse support, letting you click to switch files and scroll.

**comparison**

* mdcat is a lightweight CLI that renders Markdown to stdout in one shot. glow can both render from the CLI and run as a TUI file browser, so it suits scenarios where you browse multiple documents.
* bat focuses on syntax-highlighted file paging. glow focuses on Markdown rendering and TUI browsing. They are complementary: use bat for general files and glow for Markdown.

`glamour` lets you render markdown documents & templates on ANSI compatible terminals. You can create your own stylesheet or simply use one of the stylish defaults.

## Usage

```
import"charm.land/glamour/v2" in:= `# Hello World This is a simple example of Markdown rendering with Glamour!Check out the other examples too. Bye! ` out err:= glamour Render in "dark" fmt Print out

### Custom Renderer

```
import"charm.land/glamour/v2" r _:= glamour NewTermRenderer// wrap output at specific width (default is 80) glamour WithWordWrap 40 out err:= r Render in fmt Print out
``` [...] ### Color Downsampling

Since the renderer is designed to be "pure" and always produce the same output for the same input, it doesn't have access to the terminal's capabilities. This means that color downsampling is not performed by default. In this case, use Lip Gloss to perform downsampling before rendering:

```
import"charm.land/glamour/v2""charm.land/lipgloss/v2" r _:= glamour NewTermRenderer// wrap output at specific width (default is 80) glamour WithWordWrap 40 out err:= r Render in if err!= nil// handle error// downsample colors based on terminal capabilities. lipgloss Print out
```

## Styles

You can find all available default styles in our gallery. Want to create your own style? Learn how!

There are a few options for using a custom style: [...] There are a few options for using a custom style:

1. Call `glamour.Render(inputText, "desiredStyle")`
2. Set the `GLAMOUR_STYLE` environment variable to your desired default style or a file location for a style and call `glamour.RenderWithEnvironmentConfig(inputText)`
3. Set the `GLAMOUR_STYLE` environment variable and pass `glamour.WithEnvironmentConfig()` to your custom renderer

`glamour` lets you render [markdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markdown) documents & templates on [ANSI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code) compatible terminals. You can create your own stylesheet or simply use one of the stylish defaults.

## Usage

```
import"charm.land/glamour/v2" in:= `# Hello World This is a simple example of Markdown rendering with Glamour!Check out the [other examples](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/tree/main/examples) too. Bye! ` out err:= glamour Render in "dark" fmt Print out
```

### Custom Renderer

```
import"charm.land/glamour/v2" r _:= glamour NewTermRenderer// wrap output at specific width (default is 80) glamour WithWordWrap 40 out err:= r Render in fmt Print out
```

### Color Downsampling

Since the renderer is designed to be "pure" and always produce the same output for the same input, it doesn't have access to the terminal's capabilities. This means that color downsampling is not performed by default. In this case, use [Lip Gloss](https://github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss) to perform downsampling before rendering:

```
import"charm.land/glamour/v2""charm.land/lipgloss/v2" r _:= glamour NewTermRenderer// wrap output at specific width (default is 80) glamour WithWordWrap 40 out err:= r Render in if err!= nil// handle error// downsample colors based on terminal capabilities. lipgloss Print out
```

## Styles

You can find all available default styles in our [gallery](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/tree/main/styles/gallery). Want to create your own style? [Learn how!](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/tree/main/styles)

There are a few options for using a custom style:

1. Call `glamour.Render(inputText, "desiredStyle")`
2. Set the `GLAMOUR_STYLE` environment variable to your desired default style or a file location for a style and call `glamour.RenderWithEnvironmentConfig(inputText)`
3. Set the `GLAMOUR_STYLE` environment variable and pass `glamour.WithEnvironmentConfig()` to your custom renderer

### Word Wrapping

The `-w` flag lets you set a maximum width at which the output will be wrapped:

```
glow -w 60
```

### Paging

CLI output can be displayed in your preferred pager with the `-p` flag. This defaults to the ANSI-aware `less -r` if `$PAGER` is not explicitly set.

### Styles

You can choose a style with the `-s` flag. When no flag is provided `glow` tries to detect your terminal's current background color and automatically picks either the `dark` or the `light` style for you.

```
|
```

Alternatively you can also supply a custom JSON stylesheet:

```
glow -s mystyle.json
```

For additional usage details see:

```
glow --help
```

Check out the [Glamour Style Section](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/blob/master/styles/gallery/README.md) to find more styles. Or [make your own](https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour/tree/master/styles)!

## The Config File

If you find yourself supplying the same flags to `glow` all the time, it's probably a good idea to create a config file. Run `glow config`, which will open it in your favorite $EDITOR. Alternatively you can manually put a file named `glow.yml` in the default config path of you platform. If you're not sure where that is, please refer to `glow --help`.

Here's an example config:

```
# style name or JSON path (default "auto") # style "light" " "# mouse wheel support (TUI-mode only) # mouse true # use pager to display markdown # pager true # at which column should we word wrap? # width 80# show all files, including hidden and ignored. # all false# show line numbers (TUI-mode only) # showLineNumbers false # preserve newlines in the output # preserveNewLines false
```
